newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europarliament cool on Bosnia poll, notes "chaos".
newsitem.headline: Europarliament cool on Bosnia poll, notes "chaos".

text.p: Observers from the European Parliament said on Tuesday that "the utmost chaos" marred Bosnia's election but the poll could still pave the way to democratisation.
"The organisation of voting by non-resident electors took place in the utmost chaos," German CDU deputy Doris Pack, who led the delegation from the Strasbourg-based parliament, told reporters.
She said this could have been averted and accused the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) of "not seeing far enough".
Pack also noted huge mistakes in the registering of voters and said that the free movement of refugees had not been safeguarded.

But she added that "this election could constitute the basis for a better democracy as the new parliament will be more legitimate than what exists today and because the opposition will at least exist, which is not the case now".

A team of observers sent by the 39-nation Council of Europe, which safeguards human rights and democracy, said the poll had taken place "correctly" and paved the way for bringing into force the Dayton peace accords.
Bosnia's first elections after a 43-month war looked on Tuesday to hand victory to Croat, Moslem and Serb communal hardliners, leaving rival moderates far behind.
